draft.title: Suburbanisation and urban sprawl
card: the growth of suburbs on the edge of a city, as people move out from inner areas to new housing.
the spread of low-density development outwards from a city into land that was rural, often with houses on large blocks.
Sprawl often uses farmland and bushland on the city edge. Land that was used for crops or nature is covered by houses, roads and shops.
Distances to work, schools and services are often longer in outer suburbs. Public transport can be limited there, so car travel tends to increase.
draft.remember: Suburbs spread outwards, taking rural land and often adding car travel.

a.q: Which change is a common result of urban sprawl on the edge of a city?
opts: Farmland is replaced by housing and roads
More people live in tall towers in the centre
Car travel falls as services move closer
Rural land on the edge becomes more protected
a.why: Sprawl spreads low-density development outwards, so land once used for farming is covered by houses and roads. Tall towers in the centre describe growth upwards, which is not sprawl.
a.clue: Think about what sprawl spreads into.

b.q: A new estate of houses on large blocks opens 40 km from the centre of a city. Few buses run there, and shops and jobs are far away. What is the most likely effect on travel?
opts: Residents drive more and travel longer distances
Residents walk to work and local services
Residents mostly use trains and buses instead of cars
Residents travel less because services are nearby
b.why: In outer suburbs, jobs and services are often far away and public transport can be limited, so car travel tends to increase. Walking would suit areas with services nearby, which this estate lacks.
b.clue: Look at how far the estate is from jobs and shops.

a.best: Farmland is replaced by housing and roads

b.best: Residents drive more and travel longer distances

problems.detail: The stem already says few buses run and shops and jobs are far away. Three of the options (trains and buses, walking, services nearby) directly contradict the stem, so a student can pick the answer from the stem alone without knowing the idea. That is very easy for Year 12 HSC.

b.q: The Nguyen family moves from a flat near the centre of Perth to a new house on a large block on the city's outer edge. Which change to their daily life is most likely?
opts: They drive more and travel further to work and shops
They rely more on buses, as new estates are well served
They live at a higher density than in their old flat
Their trips get shorter, as services follow the suburbs
b.why: Outer suburbs often have longer distances to work and services, and public transport there can be limited, so car travel tends to rise. Buses are tempting, but new outer estates are often less well served than areas near the centre.
b.clue: Compare distances and public transport on the edge with the centre.

b.best: They drive more and travel further to work and shops
